author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Told partly by a credulous obsessive who believes the world is ending, PKD's one realist novel published in his lifetime dissects a disintegrating California marriage and the outsider caught inside it.
page_summary:
Jack Isidore is a 'crap artist' — a collector of pseudo-scientific facts and apocalyptic beliefs, convinced the Earth is hollow and the end is near. He moves in with his sister Fay and her husband in rural Marin County, and becomes the off-center witness to their marriage as it curdles into affairs, manipulation, and violence. The narration shifts between Jack's deranged clarity and the more conventional voices around him.

This is one of PKD's mainstream realist novels, written in the 1950s during the years he was trying to break out of the SF pulps and into literary fiction. Most of those books went unpublished in his lifetime; Confessions of a Crap Artist was the exception, appearing in the mid-1970s. Stripped of any science-fiction apparatus, it shows the same preoccupations at work — the unreliability of perception, the question of who is really the sane one, the suburban surface hiding cruelty — and it gives its most 'insane' character the steadiest grip on a certain kind of truth.

biography_events.event: PKD sends Paul Williams chapter one of CONFESSIONS OF A CRAP ARTIST for inclusion in a forthcoming printing.
In 1981, PKD wrote 33 letters to Russell Galen, turning the correspondence into a sustained discussion of the science-fiction community, religion and theology, and publishing and career pressures.
Living in Fullerton, CA ("north of Disneyland").
Written while under work pressure (started at 7:30 AM).
